article.content: In honour of Chris Wickham, the following articles are freely available for a limited period of time: Productive Forces and the Economic Logic of the Feudal Mode of Production, Author: Chris Wickham https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/16/2/article-p3_1.xml Editorial Introduction to the Symposium on “Framing the Early Middle Ages”, Author: Paul Blackledge https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p37_2.xml Framing the Early Middle Ages, Author: John Haldon https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p47_3.xml Centuries of Transition, Author: Neil Davidson https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p73_4.xml Chris Wickham’s Framing the Early Middle Ages, Author: Chris Harman https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p98_5.xml Late Antiquity to the Early Middle Ages: What Kind of Transition?, Author: Jairus Banaji https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p109_6.xml Agency and Ethics, Past and Present, Author: Kelvin Knight https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p145_7.xml Land and Power from Roman Britain to Anglo-Saxon England?, Author: John Moreland https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p175_8.xml Peasant-Based Societies in Chris Wickham’s Thought, Author: Carlos Astarita https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p194_9.xml The Problems of Comparison, Author: Chris Wickham https://brill.com/view/journals/hima/19/1/article-p221_10.xml The post Chris Wickham (1950-2026) appeared first on Historical Materialism .
